column1: # The forms .github/scripts/go_test_step_forms.py generates that rule 8 of
# the events and go test's status, or runs no go test: a pattern of form ids (fnmatch:
# a tab, and why the refusal is a known limit. The generator fails on a miss or a refusal no row
# matches and on a row that matches neither, and no row excuses a miss of a form whose runner rule 8
# cannot read, so a fix that reads one of these forms removes its row.
# Each row's last sentence says what a reading of this repository found: that no line of ci.yaml's
# run uses the form, or none that is refused for it. Rule 8 refuses every form a row names, so
# .github/scripts/check-workflow-files.sh's own clean run (0 refusals over ci.yaml's run) holds that
# again at every change; no check holds a count. The runner rows' counts were read with the rule 8
# of the change that last edited this list, the way it reads its texts (every step's run: of
# ci.yaml's run and the 166 shell scripts it reaches from them, as logical lines, so a comment or a
# heredoc of text is out), counting the lines that run the runner at a command's place. For a
# runner whose command rule 8 cannot read (eval, coproc, flock, a shell reading a pipe or a
# here-string, python3 -c, stdbuf, ionice and taskset), rule 8 refuses a line that runs one and
# names a go test, or a script that runs one, in its own words; a go test such a runner takes from
# what the line does not spell out (`eval "$cmd"`, cmd set on another line) is not seen, and no

column2: eval runs a string the shell builds when the step runs, which no reading of the step can follow: rule 8 refuses a line that runs eval and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test at a command's place. 24 lines rule 8 reads run eval, and none is refused.

coproc runs its command beside the shell, which talks to it through a pipe: rule 8 refuses a line that runs coproc and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test in the foreground. 1 line rule 8 reads runs coproc, and it is not refused.

flock runs the command after its lock file and options, which rule 8 does not read: it refuses a line that runs flock and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to take the lock on a line of its own. 3 lines rule 8 reads run flock, and none is refused.

a shell reading its script from a pipe (`| bash`) runs text another command writes when the step runs: rule 8 refuses a line that pipes into a shell and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test as a command. No line rule 8 reads pipes into a shell.

a here-string a shell takes as its script (`bash <<<`) is a word the shell expands when the step runs: rule 8 refuses a line that hands a shell a here-string and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test as a command. No line rule 8 reads hands a shell a here-string.

python3 -c runs a program in another language, here one that runs its arguments: rule 8 reads a Python script's go test argv, and no -c program, so it refuses a line that runs python3 -c and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is a script the rule reads. 59 lines rule 8 reads run python3 -c, and none is refused.

stdbuf runs the command after its options, which rule 8 does not read: it refuses a line that runs stdbuf and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test without it. No line rule 8 reads runs stdbuf.

ionice runs the command after its options, which rule 8 does not read: it refuses a line that runs ionice and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test without it. No line rule 8 reads runs ionice.

taskset runs the command after its mask or list, which rule 8 does not read: it refuses a line that runs taskset and names a go test or a script that runs one, kept or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test without it. No line rule 8 reads runs taskset.

bash does not wait for a process substitution, but a `wait $!` before another job changes `$!` waits for it and gives its status: rule 8 reads a go test in a process substitution as detached, waited or not, an over-refusal whose fix is to run the go test outside it. No go test rule 8 reads runs in a process substitution.

rule 8 reads a go test in every branch and body, as it cannot tell when the step is checked which ones the step will run: a go test no run reaches (`if false`, `false &&`, an uncalled function, an unmatched case arm, after `exit`) is refused as one that runs, an over-refusal that costs a step only the writer before that go test. No step of ci.yaml's run is refused for it: the check passes.

rule 8 reads a go word that is a variable (`"$TOOL" test`) as go whatever the step or script assigns it: which value the shell holds when the command runs is no static reading's to say, since an assignment can come after it, in another shell, a branch, a function or a sourced file, or under a name the shell builds, so `TOOL=true; "$TOOL" test` is refused, an over-refusal rather than a go test let through unrecorded. One go test of this repository has a variable go word, in packages/envoy/scripts/forced-order.sh, and the -list among its flags runs no test, so rule 8 holds it to nothing.

a `pid=$!` after `||` or `&&` runs only when the command before it decided so, which no static reading can know: rule 8 trusts a pid variable only where the assignment runs whenever the `&` did, so `pid=0; false || pid=$!; wait "$pid"` is refused though bash waits, an over-refusal whose fix is to assign the pid unconditionally. No line of this repository assigns `$!` behind `||` or `&&`.

a call of a function the shell declares may start a job of its own (`f() { sleep 0 & }`), which `$!` would then name, and rule 8 reads no function body from its call site: a call between the `&` and a `wait $!` clears `$!`, so a call of a function that starts none is refused, an over-refusal whose fix is to wait for the pid the step saved (`pid=$!`) rather than for `$!`. One line of this repository waits for `$!` and it runs no go test; no step of ci.yaml's run puts a go test in the background at all (98 lines end in `&` and none of them runs a go test).
